basis: Diabetes, progressive deafness and optic atrophy define the syndrome; neurologic HPO annotations conflict with the explicit definition and are excluded.
Defined as disease of the dermis; no additional organ involvement applies across this umbrella.
Inherited platelet dysfunction causing a bleeding disorder.
Neurodevelopmental disability defines the syndrome; minor dysmorphism does not establish other organ damage, and cardiac abnormalities are occasional.
Brain malformations and developmental impairment with arthrogryposis in 17/20; neonatal respiratory distress alone does not establish direct lung damage.
Cobalamin processing/transport defects; megaloblastic cytopenias and neurologic injury each affect >30% of symptomatic patients, with substantial subtype variation.
Familial cancer arising in the colon or rectum; associated hereditary cancer risks do not establish damage to other organs.
Hypoplastic dental enamel disorder; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Defining triad of abnormal glycosaminoglycan metabolism, cellular immunodeficiency and nephrotic syndrome; frequencies of additional organ lesions are unestablished.
Spondyloepiphyseal skeletal dysplasia with vertebral and epiphyseal abnormalities, joint restriction and skeletal deformity.
Inherited erythroid marrow failure; anemia in 5/5. Other supplied findings do not establish additional organ damage.
Benign fibrosing breast lesions; breast has no axis. Associated diabetes is a separate disease, and an immune mechanism is not established here.
Sparse hair and characteristic phalangeal/epiphyseal skeletal abnormalities define the syndrome across its principal subtypes.
Predominantly a CNS tumor; retinal tumors are a minority subtype/VHL association despite the broad HPO frequency. Neurogenic bladder does not establish direct urinary damage.
Immune-mediated rheumatoid disorder defined by polyarthritis, subchondral bone cysts and subcutaneous rheumatoid nodules.
Poxvirus infection producing cutaneous nodules. The supplied definition describes a cattle disease, not a human disease.
Intellectual disability and marked arachnodactyly define the syndrome; genital abnormalities fall outside the axes.
Generalized subcutaneous fat loss with insulin resistance; hepatic steatosis in 2/4 and intellectual impairment in approximately 80% of type 2 cases.
Autoimmune skin fibrosis; GI dysfunction ~80-90% and ILD ~50-70%. Joint damage omitted at cap; renal crisis and overt cardiac failure generally <30%.
Defined by an acute sustained loss of kidney filtration and function; additional organ damage is not inherent to the umbrella.
Acute microvesicular liver injury; direct renal dysfunction occurs in ~50% and severe coagulopathy/DIC in >30%. Encephalopathy is less consistently common.
Congenital subclavian arterial malposition; usually asymptomatic. Oesophageal or airway compression affects a minority.
Cerebral neuronal migration disorder with cortical malformation, developmental impairment, pseudobulbar palsy and epilepsy.
Malignant osteoid-producing tumor arising in bone; pulmonary metastasis is a possible later complication and does not establish common intrinsic lung involvement.
Nonsyndromic progressive sensorineural hearing loss; no additional organ disease is established.
